findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, get_discussion, get_recent_changes, semantic_search, list_blog_posts, get_blog_post, find_known_issues, explain_error, list_proposals, get_proposal · Private data: search, semantic_search, check_deprecation, get_standard, get_contract_info, check_code, find_project · Public sink: get_validators, get_blog_post · Destructive: find_code_examples.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, get_discussion, get_recent_changes, semantic_search, list_blog_posts, get_blog_post, find_known_issues, explain_error, list_proposals, get_proposal · Private data: search, semantic_search, check_deprecation, get_standard, get_contract_info, check_code, find_project · Public sink: get_validators, get_blog_post · Destructive: find_code_examples

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
